title: Density-aware callsite provenance injector and SDK middleware
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a compact, density-aware provenance stamp and injection middleware across language SDKs to improve request lineage fidelity with minimal runtime overhead. The injector emits a small provenance token (callsite hash + sampling hint + truncated timestamp) that can be propagated end-to-end and used by the runtime to stitch traces and attribute latency/error signals without requiring full-span fanout on low-cardinality paths. The feature targets edge SDKs and server frameworks where header bloat and CPU cost are sensitive (Node, Python, Go).
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware implemented in Node/Python/Go with stable API surface and unit tests
Provenance token size <= 64 bytes on average (base64 encoded) in production traffic simulations
End-to-end trace stitching success increases by >= 18% for sampled partial-traces in our synthetic microservice topology
Median added CPU per request < 0.5% and p99 added latency < 1.0ms on representative 95th percentile payloads
Rollout plan and canary gating defined; console dashboard updated with provenance-specific metrics
tasks: Spec compact provenance token format and bitpacking rules
Implement middleware for Node SDK (express/fastify adapters)
Implement middleware for Python SDK (ASGI/Werkzeug adapters)
Implement middleware for Go SDK (net/http middleware)
Add runtime parsers for provenance token and stitch heuristics in runtime-collector
Create benchmarks and perf harness with traffic density simulation
Create console dashboards (latency/error attribution, token acceptance rate)
Write rollout runbook and canary gating alerts
